SUMMARY: Epic 21 - Phase 5 decisions
DESCRIPTION: The parked items answered on 2026-10-03 (LED-214, decision OD-13) and the cookie and storage screen from OD-9. Item 7 (deficit panel without rollover) was closed as is and has no ticket.

SUMMARY: Category names are unique within their parent
USER_STORY: As a user, I want Ledger to stop me creating a second category with the same name, so reports never split one category in two.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 1). Two top-level categories cannot share a name, and two subcategories under one category cannot; the same subcategory name under different categories is allowed. Comparison is case-insensitive and ignores surrounding spaces. Existing duplicates are kept (no data is changed); only a new name or a rename is checked, so a check on insert and on a name change, not a unique index that the existing rows would fail.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Creating or renaming to a name already used under the same parent is refused with a sentence naming the clash, in the form; (b) the same subcategory name under two categories saves; (c) existing duplicates load and can be renamed; (d) enforced in the database, so an offline-queued insert that clashes reports the clash when it drains; (e) the migration applies to an empty database; (f) tests. Note (2026-10-04, plan): category writes are never queued offline (they are refused offline; only transactions and profiles are queued), so (d) is met as enforced in the database: any write that reaches it reports the clash.

SUMMARY: Import flags identical rows within one file
USER_STORY: As a user importing a statement, I want to see when two rows in the file are identical, so I can untick one if it is a mistake.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 2). Two rows with the same date, amount and description in one CSV are both imported today with no sign. Mark each such row in the preview ("Identical to row N in this file"), keep both ticked, and keep the existing duplicate-of-saved-row check as it is.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Identical rows in one file are marked in the preview and both stay ticked; (b) unticking one imports the other; (c) rows that differ in any of date, amount or description are not marked; (d) the matcher is a pure src/lib function with tests.

SUMMARY: Savings goals show on track or behind by
USER_STORY: As a user saving toward a goal, I want to see if I am on pace, so I know whether to put more in.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 3). Straight-line pace: expected = target amount x (days since the goal was created / days from creation to the target date), capped at the target. At or above expected: "On track"; below: "Behind by $X" (expected minus saved). A goal with no target date, or already complete, shows neither.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) The goal card and detail show the status per the rule; (b) no target date or complete: nothing shown; (c) a target date in the past and not reached reads "Behind by" the remaining amount; (d) the pace is a pure src/lib function with tests.

SUMMARY: A category can count as salary
USER_STORY: As a user paid under a category not named "Salary", I want to mark it as salary, so the 13th Month page counts it.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 4). Salary is matched by the category name today. Add categories.counts_as_salary (boolean, default false); a migration sets it on existing categories named Salary (as matched today), so nothing changes until the user ticks another. The category form gets a checkbox; every salary match reads the flag.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Migration sets the flag on today's matches and applies to an empty database; (b) the 13th Month page and any other salary match read the flag, not the name; (c) renaming a flagged category keeps it salary; (d) tests.

SUMMARY: Previous-period comparisons are like for like
USER_STORY: As a user part way through a cycle, I want to compare with the same days of the last cycle, so a half-month is not set against a full one.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 5). The current partial cycle is compared with the whole previous cycle today. Compare day 1 to N of the current cycle with day 1 to N of the previous one, where N is today's day in the cycle; a closed cycle still compares whole with whole. Label the comparison so it says which days it covers. Done 2026-10-04 (commit b36b5b1): likeForLikeWindows in src/lib/periodCompare.ts. Home has no previous-period delta, so (a) applies to Reports: Income, Expenses, Net change and Over budget. The label names the days when the previous window is cut ("vs Sep 1 – Sep 4").
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Every previous-period delta (Home, Reports) uses the like-for-like window for the open cycle; (b) a closed cycle is unchanged; (c) a previous cycle shorter than N days uses all of it; (d) the window is a pure src/lib function with tests.

SUMMARY: Future-dated rows count from their date
USER_STORY: As a user who enters the rent before it is due, I want it to count when it happens, so my spent-so-far is true today.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 6). The cycle runs to its end date today, so a row dated later this cycle counts at once. Spent, budgets, Overspending and Home totals count rows dated today or earlier; later rows show as scheduled (in the list and as an "upcoming" figure where a total is shown) and count once their date arrives. Reports for a past cycle are unchanged. Touches every cycle total, so list each site first. Done 2026-10-04 (commit bf117b8): countsYet in src/lib/countsYet.ts; Home income and expenses, the Budgets Spent tile and each budget show the scheduled amount apart; Activity, account pages, Home's recent rows and the Reports table mark the row Scheduled. Not changed: account balances and net worth, which the database triggers move when the row is saved (LED-251), and the Activity search sum, which adds the rows listed.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) A row dated after today in the open cycle is excluded from spent, budget, Overspending and Home totals and shown as scheduled; (b) it counts on its date with no edit; (c) closed cycles are unchanged; (d) one shared helper decides "counts yet", with tests; (e) a browser check at 390 and 1280 with a future row.

SUMMARY: Merge categories
USER_STORY: As a user with two categories that mean the same thing, I want to merge them, so their history and budgets become one.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 8). Design 8a item 5. Merge moves every transaction, subcategory and budget of the source category into the target, then deletes the source, in one SECURITY INVOKER function (patterns/atomic-write-as-an-invoker-function.md). The confirmation says how many rows move. Subcategory name clashes follow LED-233 (merged into the target's subcategory of that name). Two budgets for one category after the merge: decide in the plan and say which. Decided in the plan (2026-10-04): all budgets move and are kept, so the target may have two; the confirmation and the notice say so. The target keeps its own type, colour and salary flag.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Merge is one atomic call; a failure changes nothing; (b) the confirmation shows the counts that move; (c) no transaction is left pointing at the deleted category; (d) works for another user's category = not found (RLS); (e) refused offline; (f) migration applies to an empty database; (g) psql checks and a browser check.

SUMMARY: One Reorder control on Categories
USER_STORY: As a user, I want one clear way to reorder categories, so the list is not crowded with handles.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 8). Design 8a item 6: one Reorder control puts the list into a reorder mode (drag and keyboard move), with Done; the per-row handles go. Order saves through sort_order as today.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Reorder mode by one control, with Done; (b) keyboard reordering works and is announced; (c) the order persists; (d) checked at 390 and 1280.

SUMMARY: Sort Activity by amount
USER_STORY: As a user looking for my biggest spends, I want to sort by amount, so they come first.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 9). A Date / Amount sort control. Amount (largest first, with a reverse option) shows a flat list with the date on each row; Date brings the day groups back. Filters, search and the result bar total apply in both. The month jump rail hides while sorted by amount. Done 2026-10-04 (commit 1832126): sortByAmount and ActivitySort in src/lib/transactionWindow.ts; the result bar sort is a menu (Newest, Oldest, Largest, Smallest first). Amount compares in the default currency; a row with no rate sorts last, never one to one. The desktop month rail hides while sorted by amount; the mobile month bar stays, since it also holds Select. The sort is part of a saved filter and its link (?sort=); version 1 rows without it read as newest first, no migration. The account page keeps its two date sorts.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Amount sort orders the full filtered set (past the 1,000-row page, rules/page-reads-past-1000-rows.md); (b) flat list with dates; (c) Date restores the day groups and the scroll position resets; (d) the sort is kept with the saved filter when one is saved; (e) tests for the sort.

SUMMARY: A failed page load shows its error in about 2 s
USER_STORY: As a user on a bad connection, I want to know quickly that a page could not load, so I can retry.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 10). supabase-js retries failed GETs, so a read failure surfaces after about 8 s (LED-92). First-load reads (the read a page shows its loading state for) give up after about 2 s and show the error with Retry; background refreshes keep the longer retry. Done 2026-10-04 (commit c04bd93): readWithPolicy in src/lib/readRetry.ts turns off the supabase-js GET retries for a first load and tries once more after 1 s on a connection failure. Applied to the list reads and to the profile and exchange-rate reads Budgets waits on. Measured with rest/v1 blocked and no cache: 1.1 to 1.2 s on Activity, Accounts and Categories, 2.2 s on Budgets (was about 8 s). No time limit is put on a read.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) With reads blocked, a page's error shows within about 2 s (measured, browser check); (b) background refreshes keep retrying as before; (c) a read that succeeds on retry clears the error; (d) no read is rendered as empty (rules/read-failures-are-not-empty-states.md).

SUMMARY: Each Home widget has its own error boundary
USER_STORY: As a user, I want one broken card on Home not to take the whole page with it.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 11). Home has one boundary today. Wrap each widget; a failed widget shows "This card couldn't load" with Retry (remount) in the card's space, and the rest of Home keeps working. The error is still logged.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) A widget that throws shows the card-level message and Retry; the others render; (b) Retry remounts it; (c) the card keeps its size so the layout does not jump; (d) a test or browser check with a forced throw.

SUMMARY: A yearly budget in Overspending is labelled year to date
USER_STORY: As a user with a yearly budget, I want to see that its spend is for the year, so I do not read it as this cycle.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 in LED-214 (OD-13, item 12). The figures stay cumulative for the year; the row says so ("this year" / "year to date") wherever a yearly budget appears beside cycle budgets.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Yearly budget rows in Overspending (and the budget list, if it shows the same figure) carry the year-to-date label; (b) cycle budgets are unchanged; (c) checked at 390.

SUMMARY: Cookie and browser storage settings
USER_STORY: As a user, I want to see what Ledger keeps in my browser and clear it, so I stay in control of it.
DESCRIPTION: Decided 2026-10-03 with OD-9 (LED-189 widened). Ledger sets no tracking or advertising cookies; it keeps settings, the sign-in session, the offline queue and caches in localStorage and IndexedDB. A settings section lists each kept item in plain words (from the keys in the code), what it is for, and offers "Clear on this device" per group, with sign-out where the session is cleared. The wording comes from the cookie and storage notice approved in LED-189. Built 2026-10-04 (commit 58fa2a2): Settings → Browser storage (BrowserStorageCard), rows shared with the notice in src/lib/browserStorage.ts. (a), (b), (c) and (e) pass. (d) done after the owner approved the wording on 2026-10-04: "Removing them" on the notice links to /settings#browser-storage.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Every key the app writes is listed (checked against the source); (b) clearing a group removes exactly those keys and the app still loads; (c) clearing the offline queue warns when it holds unsynced changes; (d) linked from the cookie and storage notice; (e) checked at 390 and 1280.

SUMMARY: Hover tints drop two text colours below 4.5:1 in the light theme
USER_STORY: As a user pointing at a budget card or a transfer row, I want its text to stay readable while it is highlighted.
DESCRIPTION: Found by the first run of the LED-211 sweep script (knowledge/retros/2026-10-03-led-211-sweep-script.md), before it parked the pointer: the card or row under the pointer was measured in its hover state. Observed, light theme: (1) Budgets at 390, a budget card hovered (hover:bg-accent/20, src/pages/BudgetsPage.tsx ~1380): its "View covered transactions" link (text-primary, rgb(85,101,154)) is 4.26:1. (2) Activity at 1280, a transfer row hovered (hover:bg-accent/50, src/components/transactions/TransactionRow.tsx:106): its amount (text-transfer, rgb(61,107,143)) is 4.4:1. Resting states pass (re-run with the pointer parked: 0 below the minimum on both routes). Suggested fix: a lighter hover tint on these two surfaces, or the darker -ink variant of the text colour while hovered; then scan every hover:bg-accent site the same way.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Both texts are 4.5:1 or more while hovered, light and dark (measured with the pointer on the card and on the row); (b) other hover:bg-accent sites are scanned hovered and any failure is listed; (c) resting states unchanged.

SUMMARY: Settings shows garbled characters in the currency list and the delete button
USER_STORY: As a user choosing a currency or deleting my account, I want the text to read correctly, not as stray symbols.
DESCRIPTION: Found in passing while building LED-246. src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx holds UTF-8 text that was decoded as Windows-1252 and saved again: line 258 renders each currency option as "$ USD â€” US Dollar" (meant: an em dash) and line 707 renders the delete button's busy label as "Deletingâ€¦" (meant: an ellipsis). Two comments (:584, :645) carry the same damage. Fix: restore the characters, then add a test that fails on these sequences in src/.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) The currency options and the busy label render an em dash and an ellipsis; (b) no source file under src/ contains the mojibake sequences, enforced by a test; (c) nothing else in the file changes.

SUMMARY: Hovered primary and destructive buttons drop their label below 4.5:1
USER_STORY: As a user pointing at a button, I want its label to stay readable while it is highlighted.
DESCRIPTION: Found by the hover pass LED-246 added to the sweep (pnpm sweep --hover). The shared button variants in src/components/ui/button-variants.ts hover to a see-through fill, the same mistake as LED-246: default hover:bg-primary/85 puts --primary-foreground at 4.39:1 over a card (Add Account, Add Budget, Add Category, Add) and 4.15:1 on Settings (Save Changes, Enable Notifications), light theme; destructive dark:hover:bg-destructive/30 puts --expense at 4.27:1 (Delete My Account), dark theme. Resting states pass. Suggested fix: solid hover fills (a color-mix of the token with the surface or with black/white, as --color-surface-hover does), held by a token test.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Every button variant label holds 4.5:1 hovered, light and dark, measured with pnpm sweep --hover on all app routes at 390 and 1280; (b) a token test computes each hover fill; (c) resting states unchanged.

SUMMARY: A completed goal card dims its text below 4.5:1
USER_STORY: As a user who has completed a goal, I want its card to stay readable.
DESCRIPTION: Found while checking LED-235 with a completed goal on the local stack (the seed has none, so no sweep had seen it). SavingsGoalCard (src/pages/BudgetsPage.tsx) sets opacity-75 on the whole card when is_completed, which takes its text below the minimum: muted text ("00.00 saved", "100% of 00.00", "Mark active") 3.73:1 light and 4.44:1 dark, "Goal reached!" 3.93:1 light. A completed goal is not a disabled control, so the 3:1 disabled exemption does not apply. Suggested fix: drop the card opacity and mark completion with the existing check icon and the income-coloured bar (or a muted surface whose text is held by a token test). Also: the sweep measures emoji glyphs with the CSS text colour, which reports goal icons as failures; they render in their own colours.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) A completed goal card holds 4.5:1 for its text, light and dark, measured at 390 and 1280 with a completed goal present; (b) completion is still visible at a glance; (c) active goal cards unchanged.

SUMMARY: The auto-categorization rule form shows a category id once one is chosen
USER_STORY: As a user adding an auto-categorization rule, I want the category I picked to show by name.
DESCRIPTION: Found while validating epic 21 phase B (LED-239 hit the same issue in its merge dialog and fixed it there). In the rules dialog on Categories (src/pages/CategoriesPage.tsx), the category Select uses <SelectValue placeholder="Category" />. base-ui's Select.Value renders the raw value when no render function is given, so after choosing a category the trigger reads its uuid (seen: b930f068-1852-48f3-8f04-3178444bf878). Use the render-function form SettingsPage and the merge dialog use. Check other <SelectValue placeholder=...> sites that hold ids.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) After choosing a category the trigger shows its icon and name; (b) before choosing it shows the placeholder; (c) other Select triggers that hold ids are checked and listed, and any that show an id are fixed or filed

SUMMARY: Account balances and net worth move when a future-dated row is saved, not on its date
USER_STORY: As a user who enters the rent before it is due, I want my account balance and net worth to stay true today, so they agree with spent-so-far.
DESCRIPTION: Found while validating epic 21 phase C (LED-238). LED-238 keeps a row dated after today out of every cycle total, but account balances are kept by the database triggers, which apply the row when it is saved. Seen on the demo user: a 600 expense and a 500 income dated later in October moved Everyday Checking and net worth by -100 on save, while Home income and expenses counted neither. Needs a decision first: (a) keep stored balances as they are and show "after scheduled" beside them; (b) derive a balance as of today in the client from the stored balance less scheduled rows; (c) change the triggers to apply a row on its date (a scheduled job, a migration). Card statements and loan schedules read the same balances.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) The decision is recorded in the build order; (b) Home net worth, Accounts and Reports Net Worth agree with the chosen rule for a future row; (c) a closed cycle and rows dated today are unchanged; (d) tests for any pure helper; (e) a browser check with a future row.
